title.es: La jerga que de verdad oirás

es: Reconocer jerga y registro coloquial frecuentes (swamped, knackered, gutted, chuffed…), su equivalente neutro y el contexto en que suenan naturales o fuera de lugar.

teaching.en: A colleague might say she is swamped, but in a report to a client you would write that she is fully booked.
teaching.es: Una compañera puede decir que está desbordada, pero en un informe para un cliente escribirías que tiene la agenda completa.
teaching.explanationEs: Swamped es coloquial; el equivalente neutro es very busy o fully booked.
segments: A colleague might say she is swamped, but in a report
to a client you would write that she is fully booked.
teaching.audioText: A colleague might say she is swamped, but in a report to a client you would write that she is fully booked.

teaching.en: After a long flight, Leo says he is beat, while his British cousin, who is completely knackered, agrees.
teaching.es: Después de un vuelo largo, Leo dice que está hecho polvo, y su primo británico, que está completamente reventado, le da la razón.
teaching.explanationEs: Beat es más americano y knackered más británico; los dos significan muy cansado.
segments: After a long flight, Leo says he is beat,
while his British cousin, who is completely knackered, agrees.
teaching.audioText: After a long flight, Leo says he is beat, while his British cousin, who is completely knackered, agrees.

teaching.en: When your team loses, a friend might say bummer, but someone feeling gutted will usually say that he is very disappointed.
teaching.es: Cuando pierde tu equipo, un amigo puede decir «qué fastidio», pero quien se siente destrozado dirá normalmente que está muy decepcionado.
teaching.explanationEs: Bummer es una exclamación breve; gutted expresa una decepción fuerte y suena británico.
segments: When your team loses, a friend might say bummer, but someone
feeling gutted will usually say that he is very disappointed.
teaching.audioText: When your team loses, a friend might say bummer, but someone feeling gutted will usually say that he is very disappointed.

teaching.en: Let's chill or hang out sounds natural among friends, but in a job interview it could make you come across as careless.
teaching.es: «Let's chill» o «hang out» suena natural entre amigos, pero en una entrevista de trabajo podría hacerte parecer descuidado.
teaching.explanationEs: Come across as + adjetivo: la impresión que das. El registro elegido cambia esa impresión.
segments: Let's chill or hang out sounds natural among friends, but in
a job interview it could make you come across as careless.
teaching.audioText: Let's chill or hang out sounds natural among friends, but in a job interview it could make you come across as careless.

teaching.en: Awesome and no worries are friendly in a text message, but an apology to a client deserves something more formal.
teaching.es: Awesome y no worries resultan cordiales en un mensaje de texto, pero una disculpa a un cliente merece algo más formal.
teaching.explanationEs: Awesome sustituye a excellent; no worries a that is quite all right. Ambos son informales.
segments: Awesome and no worries are friendly in a text message,
but an apology to a client deserves something more formal.
teaching.audioText: Awesome and no worries are friendly in a text message, but an apology to a client deserves something more formal.

teaching.en: A British mate might say he is chuffed about his promotion, while an American friend would say he is thrilled.
teaching.es: Un amigo británico podría decir que está muy contento con su ascenso, mientras que uno estadounidense diría que está emocionado.
teaching.explanationEs: Chuffed es muy británico; mate, en la misma línea, se usa entre amigos.
segments: A British mate might say he is chuffed about his
promotion, while an American friend would say he is thrilled.
teaching.audioText: A British mate might say he is chuffed about his promotion, while an American friend would say he is thrilled.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje dice lo mismo en registro neutro?

choices.text: I am very happy and relaxed, so I cannot come tonight; could we meet on Saturday?
I am very busy and exhausted, so I cannot come tonight; could we meet on Saturday?
I am very busy and angry, so I cannot come tonight; could we meet on Saturday?

feedback.es: Swamped equivale a very busy y knackered a exhausted; las otras opciones cambian el estado de ánimo del hablante.

hint.es: Traduce cada palabra coloquial por su equivalente neutro.

origin.text: Sorry mate, I'm swamped at work and completely knackered, so I'm going to skip tonight. Bummer, I know! Let's hang out on Saturday instead.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estaba destrozada porque esperaba aprobar.»

feedback.es: Gutted es la palabra británica para una decepción fuerte.

origin.text: Mia failed the exam by two points. She was absolutely ___ about it, because she had hoped to pass with a good mark.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Awesome queda bien en un mensaje, pero no en un informe.»

answer.text: Awesome is fine in a text but not in a report

feedback.es: El registro decide dónde cabe la palabra: un mensaje entre amigos sí, un informe no.

hint.es: Primero la palabra coloquial, y al final el contraste con not in a report.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prefiere hacer Tom esa noche.

choices.text: Go out and celebrate getting the job.
Catch up on work he has fallen behind with.
Stay in and rest after his night shift.

feedback.es: Tom está agotado tras el turno de noche y prefiere relajarse en casa; la buena noticia del empleo llega después, y nadie habla de trabajo atrasado.

origin.audio: I met Tom at the station. He said he was completely knackered after the night shift, and that he would rather chill at home than go out. I said no worries, mate, and we left it there. Then he texted me: awesome news, he is chuffed, because he has got the job.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión coloquial con su significado.

feedback.es: Las cuatro expresiones se oyen entre amigos: decepción, alegría, planes informales y quitar importancia.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje es adecuado para declinar una entrevista de trabajo?

choices.text: I am afraid I cannot attend on Tuesday, as I am fully booked that day.
Sorry mate, I'm swamped on Tuesday, so I'll skip it, no worries!
Bummer, but I'm knackered on Tuesday, so can we chill about it?

feedback.es: A un empleador se le escribe en registro neutro; las otras dos mezclan jerga de amigos y dan mala impresión.

origin.text: You are writing to the manager of a company to say that you cannot attend Tuesday's interview. Which message is best?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la hablante sobre su nueva compañera de apartamento.

choices.text: She thinks her flatmate is rude to the landlord.
She likes her, but finds her energy tiring.
She would like to move out because of her flatmate's plans.

feedback.es: Elogia a su compañera, pero el humor final (seguir hablando a través de la puerta) revela que su energía la cansa.

origin.audio: My new flatmate is a lovely girl, really, and a proper laugh. She is chuffed to bits with the flat, and she calls everyone mate, even the landlord. But she does come across as a bit much at seven in the morning. Last Sunday I was knackered, and she wanted to hang out and plan the whole week. I said no worries, I'll just lie down for ten minutes. Honestly, I am not complaining; I am only saying that some people are not ready for a whole week of plans before breakfast. Half an hour later, she was still talking to me through the door.

prompt.es: ¿Qué impresión probable causa este correo en el cliente?

choices.text: That the sender is concealing the true reason for the delay.
That the sender has too much work and expects the client to help.
That the sender treats the client and the delay too lightly.

feedback.es: El retraso se explica, pero el registro de amigos hace que el cliente pueda sentir que se le toma poco en serio; la razón no se oculta ni se le pide ayuda.

origin.text: Hi Mr Hughes, sorry mate, the report is going to be late. I'm completely swamped this week, and I'm knackered, to be honest. Bummer, I know! No worries if you're annoyed, we can hang out on Friday and sort it out. I'll send you everything as soon as I can, I promise, and I'll bring the coffee.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tras tres semanas de resfriado, estaba agotadísimo y durmió doce horas.»

feedback.es: Knackered es el coloquial británico para agotado; beat es la variante más americana.

origin.text: After three weeks of a bad cold, he was absolutely ___ and slept for twelve hours without a break.

prompt.es: Reescribe el mensaje en registro neutro para un cliente.

answer.text: I am very busy this week and extremely tired, so I am afraid I cannot attend on Thursday. I apologise for that. Could we meet on Saturday instead?
accepted: I am very busy this week and extremely tired, so I am afraid I cannot attend on Thursday. I apologise for that. Could we meet on Saturday instead?
I am fully booked this week and exhausted, so unfortunately I cannot come on Thursday. I am sorry about that. Would Saturday suit you instead?

feedback.es: El registro neutro sustituye swamped y knackered por equivalentes formales y convierte el plan en una propuesta educada.

origin.text: Hey mate, I'm swamped this week and completely knackered, so I'll skip Thursday. Bummer, I know! Let's hang out on Saturday instead, no worries?

prompt.es: ¿Qué busca el autor con este mensaje a un amigo?

choices.text: To decline this invitation kindly while showing he still wants to meet.
To ask his friend to change the date because his gran is ill.
To excuse himself from the group because he is too tired to go out.

feedback.es: Rechaza esa fecha con una razón y propone alternativas y comida: declina con amabilidad y mantiene la relación; no pide cambiar la fecha por enfermedad ni se aparta del grupo.

origin.text: Thanks for the invite! I'd love to hang out, but I've promised my gran a visit, and then I'll probably be knackered. No worries if the plan changes, though: I'm up for a chill evening any time next week, and I'll bring the snacks. Say hi to everybody from me, and tell them that I am thinking of them.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esa palabra parecería demasiado informal para un cliente.»

answer.text: That word would come across as too casual for a client

feedback.es: Come across as + adjetivo describe la impresión que causa una palabra en un contexto formal.

prompt.es: Completa: «No pasa nada, amigo; le podría pasar a cualquiera.»

feedback.es: No worries es la respuesta habitual, cordial e informal, a una disculpa.

origin.text: Sorry about the mix-up, it was entirely my fault. No ___, mate; it could have happened to anyone.

es: Usar bloques léxicos frecuentes del habla (the thing is, to be fair, mind you, come to think of it, for what it's worth…) para dar fluidez, con gerundio e infinitivo correctos.

usesVocabulary: to cut a long story short

vocabulary.en: to cut a long story short

teaching.en: Apparently, the landlord is selling the building; the thing is, nobody has told the tenants anything yet.
teaching.es: Por lo visto, el casero vende el edificio; la cuestión es que nadie les ha dicho nada a los inquilinos todavía.
teaching.explanationEs: Apparently cuenta lo que has oído; the thing is presenta el problema y va seguido de una frase completa.
segments: Apparently, the landlord is selling the building; the thing
is, nobody has told the tenants anything yet.
teaching.audioText: Apparently, the landlord is selling the building; the thing is, nobody has told the tenants anything yet.

teaching.en: Basically, she forgot to book the venue; to be fair, nobody reminded her, and to be honest, I forgot too.
teaching.es: Básicamente, olvidó reservar el local; siendo justos, nadie se lo recordó, y para ser sincero, yo también me olvidé.
teaching.explanationEs: Forget + to + verbo: no hacer algo pendiente. To be fair concede; to be honest admite.
segments: Basically, she forgot to book the venue; to be fair,
nobody reminded her, and to be honest, I forgot too.
teaching.audioText: Basically, she forgot to book the venue; to be fair, nobody reminded her, and to be honest, I forgot too.

teaching.en: Anyway, it's not like I mind helping, but come to think of it, I spent all of last weekend moving boxes.
teaching.es: En fin, no es que me importe ayudar, pero ahora que lo pienso, pasé todo el fin de semana pasado moviendo cajas.
teaching.explanationEs: Mind + gerundio (mind helping). Come to think of it introduce una idea que se recuerda de repente.
segments: Anyway, it's not like I mind helping, but come to think
of it, I spent all of last weekend moving boxes.
teaching.audioText: Anyway, it's not like I mind helping, but come to think of it, I spent all of last weekend moving boxes.

teaching.en: She stopped talking to me straight afterwards; mind you, she had apologised twice, as a matter of fact, so basically we are fine.
teaching.es: Dejó de hablarme justo después; eso sí, se había disculpado dos veces, de hecho, así que básicamente estamos bien.
teaching.explanationEs: Stop + gerundio = dejar de hacer algo; stop + to + verbo = pararse para hacerlo. As a matter of fact refuerza un dato.
segments: She stopped talking to me straight afterwards; mind you, she had apologised
twice, as a matter of fact, so basically we are fine.
teaching.audioText: She stopped talking to me straight afterwards; mind you, she had apologised twice, as a matter of fact, so basically we are fine.

teaching.en: To cut a long story short, he apologised, and for what it's worth, I believed him; anyway, that is all in the past.
teaching.es: Resumiendo, se disculpó, y por si sirve de algo, le creí; en fin, todo eso ya es pasado.
teaching.explanationEs: To cut a long story short resume; for what it's worth ofrece una opinión con modestia.
segments: To cut a long story short, he apologised, and for what it's
worth, I believed him; anyway, that is all in the past.
teaching.audioText: To cut a long story short, he apologised, and for what it's worth, I believed him; anyway, that is all in the past.

teaching.en: Basically, chunks buy you thinking time; use them sparingly, or you may sound vague rather than fluent.
teaching.es: Básicamente, los bloques te dan tiempo para pensar; úsalos con moderación, o podrías sonar vago en lugar de fluido.
teaching.explanationEs: Un bloque debe ayudar a hablar con claridad, no llenar silencios sin sentido.
segments: Basically, chunks buy you thinking time; use them sparingly,
or you may sound vague rather than fluent.
teaching.audioText: Basically, chunks buy you thinking time; use them sparingly, or you may sound vague rather than fluent.

prompt.es: Completa: «Siendo justos, ella intentó llamarte dos veces.»

feedback.es: To be fair concede un punto a favor de alguien antes de seguir.

hint.es: Adjetivo de «justo» dentro del bloque que concede algo.

origin.text: You are upset that your sister missed your party. Your brother says: To be ___, she did try to call you twice, and she was stuck at work.

prompt.es: ¿Qué bloque cierra mejor esta conversación?

choices.text: Mind you, I should get back to work.
Basically, I should get back to work.
Anyway, I should get back to work.

feedback.es: Anyway corta el tema anterior y permite pasar a otra cosa; mind you y basically no sirven para despedirse.

hint.es: Busca el bloque que cierra o cambia de tema.

origin.text: Leo and Mia have talked about the holiday for twenty minutes, and there is nothing more to say. Mia looks at her watch and wants to get back to her desk.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La cuestión es que olvidé reservar la mesa.»

answer.text: The thing is, I forgot to book the table

feedback.es: The thing is abre el problema y forget + to + verbo dice qué no se hizo.

hint.es: Empieza con el bloque que presenta el problema.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra la hablante ante el cierre de la tienda.

choices.text: She is not surprised and feels little sense of loss.
She is not surprised, but she regrets that the shop never had customers.
She is surprised by the news, though she never liked the prices.

feedback.es: Dice que no le sorprende, que nunca vio clientes y que no echará de menos los precios: es indiferente, no lamenta la falta de clientes ni se sorprende.

origin.audio: Apparently, the shop is closing down. Mind you, I am not surprised; to be honest, I never saw more than two customers in there. Anyway, it's not like I will miss the prices.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada bloque con su función en la conversación.

pairs.es: Conceder algo a favor del otro
Añadir un matiz a lo dicho

feedback.es: Cada bloque cumple una función distinta: problema, concesión, matiz y recuerdo repentino.

pairs.es: Conceder algo a favor del otro
Añadir un matiz a lo dicho

prompt.es: Completa: «Recuerdo haber cerrado la ventana antes de salir.»

feedback.es: Remember + gerundio recuerda algo que ya se hizo; remember + to sería algo pendiente.

origin.text: It cannot have been me who left the window open. I remember ___ it before I left the house, and I checked it twice.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el hablante sobre las excusas de su hermano.

choices.text: He accepts the excuses and is glad that his brother will visit on Sunday.
He grants a few points but expects his brother to let Gran down again.
He thinks his brother forgot because he is too busy with work.

feedback.es: Concede algún punto (to be fair), pero señala que pasó un día entero sin llamada y que la promesa viene de alguien que ya olvidó una en marzo: espera que vuelva a fallarle a la abuela.

origin.audio: I asked my brother whether he had called Gran on her birthday. Well, apparently, the thing is, his phone had no battery, and, to be fair, he was stuck on the motorway for three hours. Mind you, it was four o'clock when I asked him, and the birthday was yesterday. Come to think of it, he did say in March that he would remember to call her. Anyway, for what it's worth, he has now promised to drive over on Sunday. To cut a long story short, Gran has waited a whole day for that call, and I suspect she will be waiting on Sunday as well.

prompt.es: Completa: «Básicamente, terminé casi todo, pero falta revisar las cifras.»

feedback.es: Basically resume lo esencial antes de dar el detalle que falta.

origin.text: Did you finish the report? ___, I did most of it, but I still need to check the figures before I send it.

prompt.es: ¿Para qué dice Sara «to be fair» en esta conversación?

choices.text: To warn Leo that the manager will reject his next plan too.
To excuse the manager completely and tell Leo to drop the matter.
To soften Leo's complaint with a point in the manager's favour.

feedback.es: To be fair introduce un dato favorable a la directora que matiza la queja de Leo sin negarla; Sara no la excusa del todo ni pide que lo deje.

origin.text: Leo spent the coffee break complaining about the new manager, who had rejected his plan without a word of thanks. Sara listened, then said quietly: «To be fair, she has been here three weeks and she has a budget problem.» Leo looked at his cup and said that, actually, it was only a plan.

prompt.es: Explica a Tom por qué faltaste a su fiesta usando bloques del habla.

answer.text: The thing is, I was feeling ill, and to be honest, I forgot to call you. Anyway, I am sorry, and for what it's worth, I would love to see you this weekend.
accepted: The thing is, I was feeling ill, and to be honest, I forgot to call you. Anyway, I am sorry, and for what it's worth, I would love to see you this weekend.
The thing is, I was exhausted after work. To be honest, I should have called you. Anyway, let's meet on Saturday; for what it's worth, I will bring the cake.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta usa tres bloques: The thing is para el problema, to be honest para admitir y anyway para cerrar.

origin.text: Tom te pregunta por qué no fuiste a su fiesta. Respóndele con tres bloques: The thing is…, To be honest… y Anyway… (o for what it's worth…).

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el hablante sobre su relación con ella?

choices.text: He cares about her but is frustrated that she hides problems.
He is annoyed that she is always too busy to talk to him.
He admits that he hides problems too, and he blames himself.

feedback.es: Niega que le caiga mal, le frustra que ella oculte sus problemas y reconoce que él hace lo mismo: hay cariño y reproche, no autoinculpación total ni enojo por falta de tiempo.

origin.text: «It's not like I dislike her,» he said, stirring his tea for the third time. «The thing is, she always says she's fine, and then I find out a week later that she wasn't. Mind you, I'm no better. I do exactly the same thing with my own problems, and then I wonder why nobody tells me anything.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para ser sincero, dejé de comer azúcar el año pasado.»

answer.text: To be honest, I stopped eating sugar last year
accepted: To be honest, I stopped eating sugar last year
I stopped eating sugar last year, to be honest

feedback.es: Stop + gerundio significa dejar de hacer algo, y to be honest introduce una opinión sincera.

prompt.es: Completa: «Olvidó pagar la factura, así que le cortaron la luz.»

feedback.es: Forget + to + verbo significa olvidar hacer algo pendiente, como pagar la factura.

origin.text: Sara is usually very careful with money. This time she forgot ___ the bill, so the power was cut off for two days.

title.es: Notas de voz desde el extranjero

es: Deducir el significado de palabras desconocidas en notas de voz con habla natural, apoyándote en una pista del contexto (get the gist of, make out, pick up on).

teaching.en: You can hardly catch every word of a fast voice note, but you can still get the gist of it from context.
teaching.es: Apenas puedes captar cada palabra de una nota de voz rápida, pero aun así puedes entender la idea general por el contexto.
teaching.explanationEs: Hardly = casi no; get the gist of: entender lo esencial sin conocer cada palabra.
segments: You can hardly catch every word of a fast voice note,
but you can still get the gist of it from context.
teaching.audioText: You can hardly catch every word of a fast voice note, but you can still get the gist of it from context.

teaching.en: If you hear that a flat is cramped and that two suitcases fill the floor, you can make out the meaning without a dictionary.
teaching.es: Si oyes que un apartamento es estrecho y que dos maletas llenan el suelo, puedes deducir el significado sin diccionario.
teaching.explanationEs: Cramped describe un sitio sin espacio; make out: llegar a entender algo con esfuerzo.
segments: If you hear that a flat is cramped and that two suitcases
fill the floor, you can make out the meaning without a dictionary.
teaching.audioText: If you hear that a flat is cramped and that two suitcases fill the floor, you can make out the meaning without a dictionary.

teaching.en: Streets full of buses, markets and shouting sellers tell you that bustling describes a busy and noisy place.
teaching.es: Calles llenas de autobuses, mercados y vendedores que gritan te dicen que bustling describe un lugar concurrido y ruidoso.
teaching.explanationEs: El contexto da la pista: varios elementos activos alrededor de la palabra.
segments: Streets full of buses, markets and shouting sellers tell
you that bustling describes a busy and noisy place.
teaching.audioText: Streets full of buses, markets and shouting sellers tell you that bustling describes a busy and noisy place.

teaching.en: Listeners who pick up on a dropping voice will realise that she is homesick, even if she never says so.
teaching.es: Quien se fija en una voz que baja se dará cuenta de que ella extraña su casa, aunque nunca lo diga.
teaching.explanationEs: Pick up on: captar una señal; el tono de voz también es una pista.
segments: Listeners who pick up on a dropping voice will realise
that she is homesick, even if she never says so.
teaching.audioText: Listeners who pick up on a dropping voice will realise that she is homesick, even if she never says so.

teaching.en: He looked bewildered by the ticket machine, and it dawned on me that he had never seen one before.
teaching.es: Parecía desconcertado ante la máquina de boletos, y caí en la cuenta de que nunca había visto una antes.
teaching.explanationEs: It dawned on me that…: darse cuenta de algo de repente.
segments: He looked bewildered by the ticket machine, and it dawned
on me that he had never seen one before.
teaching.audioText: He looked bewildered by the ticket machine, and it dawned on me that he had never seen one before.

teaching.en: After a week of grey drizzle in a sketchy area, I began to lose track of the days.
teaching.es: Tras una semana de llovizna gris en una zona de mala pinta, empecé a perder la cuenta de los días.
teaching.explanationEs: Drizzle es lluvia fina; sketchy, de aspecto poco fiable; lose track of + algo.
segments: After a week of grey drizzle in a sketchy
area, I began to lose track of the days.
teaching.audioText: After a week of grey drizzle in a sketchy area, I began to lose track of the days.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué significa «cramped» según la pista del mensaje.

choices.text: Very small, with no room to move.
Very expensive for that part of town.
Very dark and cold in winter.

feedback.es: Poder tocar las dos paredes y guardar la maleta bajo la cama son pistas de un espacio mínimo.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que puede hacer con las manos.

origin.audio: Hi! So, the flat is tiny, honestly cramped: I can touch both walls with my hands, and my suitcase lives under the bed. But the street is lovely, and there is a little market downstairs.

prompt.es: Completa: «Era solo una llovizna, así que no abrí el paraguas.»

feedback.es: Drizzle es lluvia fina y ligera: apenas moja, por eso no hace falta el paraguas.

hint.es: Sustantivo para una lluvia muy fina.

origin.text: It was only a light ___, so I did not even open my umbrella, but the pavement was wet when I arrived at the station.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Apenas te oigo con todo este ruido.»

answer.text: I can hardly hear you over this noise

feedback.es: Hardly va entre el modal y el verbo: can hardly hear significa casi no oír.

hint.es: Hardly se coloca entre can y hear.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué se siente desconcertado el hablante.

choices.text: He bought the wrong ticket because the woman gave him bad advice.
He cannot make sense of the signs or the machine.
He is lost because he cannot find the station.

feedback.es: Las señales ilegibles y la máquina con cuarenta botones explican su desconcierto; además, una mujer sí le ayudó, así que nadie lo engañó.

origin.audio: Hi Leo, it's Tom. I'm writing from the new place, and I have to say I'm a bit bewildered. The signs are all in a language I can't read, and the ticket machine has about forty buttons. I pressed every one and got a receipt for a bus I did not need. Anyway, a woman laughed kindly and showed me. I'll call later.

prompt.es: ¿Qué significa «sketchy» en el mensaje de Mar?

choices.text: Looking abandoned, as if it had closed for good.
Looking cheap, with poor and old decoration.
Looking unsafe or not to be trusted.

feedback.es: Luces rotas, una discusión en la puerta y nadie en la barra son pistas de un lugar poco fiable.

origin.text: Mar's message: «I didn't go into the bar on the corner. Sketchy, honestly: broken lights, two men arguing outside and nobody behind the counter. I'll stick to the café near the station.»

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el significado de la palabra destacada.

pairs: The streets were bustling: buses, markets, people shouting.
I feel homesick: I keep looking at photos of my mother's kitchen.
The flat was cramped: two suitcases filled the floor.
The café looked sketchy: broken windows and nobody inside.

feedback.es: En cada frase, el resto de la oración da la pista que permite deducir la palabra.

pairs: The streets were bustling: buses, markets, people shouting.

It drizzled all Tuesday, and on Wednesday a man in a sketchy jacket offered to sell me a bus pass, which I politely refused. Honestly, I felt bewildered for three days. answer.text: Sunday. I landed at nine, and the taxi driver talked for the whole ride. I was completely knackered, so I went straight to bed. Monday. Monday. I landed late, and the airport was chaos. On Tuesday I could not figure out the ticket machine, so I asked a man to rephrase what he was saying, and we muddled through with gestures. Bummer, I missed my bus! On Wednesday, to be honest, I felt homesick, but I managed to sort out my room with the landlady. Thursday. I am slowly getting the hang of the coffee shop, and the waiter says my accent is nice. Mind you, he says it to everybody. By Saturday I had pretty much settled in, and on Sunday I slept until noon. Anyway, it was a tiring but awesome first week. On Friday, a neighbour invited me for tea, and I could only make out half of what she said, but I got the gist of it, and we had a lovely evening.
